title: Motion in one dimension
summary: How do position, velocity, and acceleration change along a straight line?
olay.h: Which lands first, the hammer or the feather?
olay.p: Apollo 15 astronaut David Scott dropped a hammer and a falcon feather from the same height at the same moment. The Moon has no air, so both hit the ground together.
cards.0.p: Position is where you are relative to a starting point. Displacement (Δx = xfinal − xinitial) is a quantity with direction. Distance is the total length of the path you travel.
cards.0.key: If you go 50 m forward and then 20 m back, the distance is 70 m but the displacement is +30 m. Distance is never smaller than |Δx|.
cards.1.p: Average speed is distance divided by time. Average velocity is Δx / Δt, and it has a direction. Both are measured in m/s.
cards.1.key: Average speed is not the average of the speeds. If you cover half the distance at 40 km/h and the other half at 60 km/h, your average speed is 48 km/h.
cards.2.p: On a position-time graph, the slope between two points is the average velocity. The slope of the tangent at a single point is the instantaneous velocity.
cards.2.key: On an x–t graph, slope = velocity. A car's speedometer shows instantaneous speed.
cards.3.h: Acceleration: how fast does velocity change?
cards.3.p: Acceleration tells you how much the velocity changes each second. It is a = Δv / Δt, measured in m/s². An acceleration that points opposite to the velocity slows the car down.
cards.3.svg#9: velocity grows 4 m/s each second, so the gaps widen
cards.3.key: A car that goes from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 s has an acceleration of a = 20 / 5 = 4 m/s².
cards.4.p: If the velocity is constant, the acceleration is zero and Δx = v·t. The position-time graph is a sloped line and the velocity-time graph is a horizontal line.
cards.4.key: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the displacement.
cards.5.h: Velocity and position at constant acceleration
cards.5.p: At constant acceleration, the velocity grows by the same amount each second, so v = v<sub>0</sub> + a·t. The area under the graph is a rectangle plus a triangle. That gives Δx = v<sub>0</sub>·t + ½·a·t².
cards.5.key: If v<sub>0</sub> = 2 m/s, a = 2 m/s², and t = 4 s, then Δx = 8 + 16 = 24 m.
cards.6.h: The equation without time: braking distance
cards.6.p: When you don't know the time, use v² = v0² + 2·a·Δx. For this car, 0 = 400 − 10·Δx, so it stops in 40 m.
cards.6.key: The slope of a velocity-time graph is the acceleration. The area, ½ · 20 · 4 = 40 m, gives the same answer.
cards.6.etk.soru: Change the car's speed and its braking acceleration. When the speed doubles, how many times longer is the braking distance?
cards.6.once.soru: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes and slows by 5 m/s every second. How many seconds does it take to stop?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: The velocity drops 5 m/s each second, so the car stops in 20 / 5 = 4 s. How many meters does it travel in that time?
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: The velocity drops 5 m/s each second. How many 5s does it take to get from 20 down to 0?
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: You don't multiply 20 by 5 here. A velocity of 20 m/s drops by 5 m/s each second.
cards.7.p: Without air resistance, every object falls with the same acceleration. It is g ≈ 9.8 m/s², and we round it to 10 in calculations. For an object dropped from rest, v = g·t and h = ½·g·t².
cards.7.key: After 1 s the velocity is 10 m/s and the object has fallen 5 m. After 2 s the velocity is 20 m/s and it has fallen 20 m.
cards.8.p: An object thrown downward also accelerates at g, but its velocity starts at v0. So v = v0 + g·t and h = v0·t + ½·g·t².
cards.8.key: A stone thrown at 5 m/s reaches 25 m/s in 2 s and travels 30 m.
cards.8.once.soru: A stone is thrown downward at 5 m/s. What is its velocity after 2 s?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: The acceleration is still g, so the velocity grows 10 m/s each second. That gives 5 + 10 · 2 = 25 m/s.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: That would be the velocity of a stone dropped from rest. This stone already started at 5 m/s.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: That is the velocity after 1 s. In 2 s, 10 m/s is added twice.
cards.9.p: An object thrown upward slows by 10 m/s each second, so v = v<sub>0</sub> − g·t. At the top its velocity is zero, but its acceleration is still g.
cards.9.svg#5: at the top v = 0, a = g
cards.9.key: The time to the top is v<sub>0</sub>/g and the maximum height is v<sub>0</sub>²/(2g). The way down takes as long as the way up, and the object returns at the same speed.
cards.10.p: The slope of a position-time graph gives velocity. The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration. The area under a velocity-time graph gives Δx, and the area under an acceleration-time graph gives Δv. Area below the axis counts as negative.
cards.10.key: If velocity and acceleration have the same sign, the object speeds up. If they have opposite signs, it slows down. So negative acceleration does not always mean slowing down.
cards.11.p: Motion comes in three forms. A runner moves in translation, a propeller in rotation, and a swing in vibration. Motion is also uniform or non-uniform, depending on whether the velocity changes.
cards.11.key: Vibration is moving back and forth on either side of an equilibrium point.
cards.11.once.soru: How does a rolling wheel move?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: The center of the wheel travels from one place to another, and the wheel also turns around its own axis. Both motions happen at once.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: Look at a point on the rim of the wheel. It also goes around the center.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: The wheel is not spinning in place. Its center travels from one place to another.
cards.12.p:
• Displacement is a vector and distance is a scalar. Velocity is Δx/Δt and acceleration is Δv/Δt.
• At constant acceleration, v = v0 + at and Δx = v0t + ½at².
• The slope of a position-time graph gives velocity. The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration, and its area gives Δx.
• In free fall the acceleration is g.
quiz.0.q: The car goes 35 m forward from the starting point, then 15 m back. Move the car to its final position.
quiz.0.e: The final position is x = 35 − 15 = 20 m. The displacement is +20 m, and the distance traveled is 35 + 15 = 50 m.
quiz.1.q: On a car's v–t graph, the velocity rises steadily from 0 to 8 m/s between 0 and 4 s, then stays at 8 m/s between 4 and 6 s. What is the car's displacement in 6 s, in meters?
quiz.1.e: Displacement is the area under the velocity-time graph. The triangle has an area of ½·4·8 = 16 m and the rectangle 2·8 = 16 m. The total is 32 m.
quiz.2.q: What do you read from each graph? Match them.
quiz.2.e: A slope tells you how fast the quantity on the vertical axis changes. On a position-time graph that is velocity, and on a velocity-time graph it is acceleration. An area gives a product. v·t is displacement and a·t is the change in velocity.
quiz.3.q: With no air resistance, a ball is thrown upward at 30 m/s. What is the maximum height it reaches, in meters? (g = 10 m/s²)
quiz.3.e: At the top the velocity is zero, so h = v₀² / (2g) = 900 / 20 = 45 m. The climb takes 30 / 10 = 3 s.
quiz.3.y.1: If you got 90, you forgot the 2 in the denominator. The correct form is h = v₀² / (2g) = 900 / 20.
quiz.3.y.2: 30 is the number for the initial velocity. The height comes from v₀² / (2g).
quiz.3.y.3: If you got 15, you only divided the initial velocity by 2. The height is v₀² / (2g) = 45 m.
A:ozet: Try it first, then learn its name. Drive the car, drag the graph, and throw the ball.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Drag the car to the yellow flag.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: The car is 30 m from the start, so its position is x = 30 m. Position is always given relative to a starting point.
A:adimlar.1.metin: You can measure a trip in two ways. One is where you started and where you ended up. The other is how far you traveled in total.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: The car will go 40 m forward, then 30 m back. What do you think its displacement (Δx) is, in meters?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Displacement only looks at the first and last positions, so Δx = 10 − 0 = +10 m. The total length traveled is the distance, and it is 40 + 30 = 70 m.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: 70 m is the total length the car traveled. That is the distance.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: −30 m is only the displacement on the way back. Don't forget the first 40 m.
A:adimlar.2.metin: The camera takes one frame every second. A moves 5 m each second. Set B's velocity and press play. Make the two cars travel side by side.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: Both cars move 5 m each second, so v = Δx / Δt = 25 m / 5 s = 5 m/s. Equal velocities mean equally spaced frames.
A:adimlar.3.metin: As the car moves, it plots its position on the graph at every moment. Pick two different velocities and play both.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: What does the faster car's line look like?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The fast car covers more ground each second, so its line rises faster. The slope of a position-time graph is the velocity.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Look at the graphs. Which line is higher at second 5?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The two lines don't end at the same place. Which one ends higher?
A:adimlar.4.metin: The car starts from rest and steps on the gas. Pick an acceleration and press play.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: Which of these strips looks like the frames taken each second?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Equal gaps mean constant velocity. A car that speeds up covers more ground each second.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: As the velocity grows, the car covers more ground each second, so the frames spread apart. The velocity-time graph also rises as a straight line.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: If the gaps shrink, the car is slowing down. How did the frames above spread?
A:adimlar.5.metin: The car moves at a constant 5 m/s. Drag the handle on the graph to move time forward and bring the car to the flag.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: The car traveled 20 m in 4 s. The shaded rectangle also has an area of 5 · 4 = 20. So the area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance traveled.
A:adimlar.6.metin: Now the car starts from rest and speeds up by 2 m/s each second. Drag the handle and bring the car to the flag at 16 m.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: After 4 s the velocity was 8 m/s. The shaded triangle has an area of ½ · 8 · 4 = 16 m. The area rule also works for a car that speeds up.
A:adimlar.7.metin: In a tube with the air pumped out, a 5 kg cannonball and a 1 g feather will be dropped at the same moment.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.soru: Which one hits the ground first?
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The cannonball is pulled with a larger force, but its mass is larger by the same factor. So its acceleration is the same as the feather's.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: What slows a feather in air is air resistance. This tube has no air.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Without air, every object falls with the same acceleration. Both fell 20 m in 2 s. The gap between the marks grew each time, so they sped up as they fell.
A:adimlar.8.metin: Drag the velocity arrow upward to choose the launch speed, then press play. Make the ball rise to exactly 20 m.
A:adimlar.8.gorev.tamam: The ball thrown at 20 m/s slowed by 10 m/s each second, stopped after 2 s, and reached 20 m. Then it came back in the same time, at the same speed.
A:adimlar.9.baslik: Read the motion from a graph
A:adimlar.9.metin: This time the graph is ready. Press play and watch the car. What happens in the yellow region?
A:adimlar.9.gorev.soru: What is the car doing between seconds 2 and 4, where the graph is flat?
A:adimlar.9.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The position does not change, and x stays at 30 m. A horizontal line has zero slope, so the velocity is zero. In the last part the line goes down, so the car is coming back.
A:adimlar.9.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A car moving at constant velocity changes position every second, so its line is sloped. Is x changing here?
A:adimlar.9.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The position graph of a car that speeds up is a curve that gets steeper. Press play and watch the car.
A:kapanis.0: Position is where you are relative to the start. Displacement is Δx = xfinal − xinitial.
A:kapanis.1: Distance is the total length traveled. If you turn back, the distance is larger than Δx.
A:kapanis.2: Velocity is displacement divided by time (v = Δx / Δt), and it is the slope of the position-time graph. Total distance divided by time is called speed. On a trip where you turn back, the two are different.
A:kapanis.3: Acceleration is the change in velocity each second. For a car that speeds up, the frames spread apart.
A:kapanis.4: If the position-time graph is flat, the car is stopped. If it goes down, the car is moving back.
